citation: Miller, S., Biggart, A., Sloan, S., & O'Hare, L. (2017). Success for All: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluators: Centre for Evidence and Social Innovation, Queen's University Belfast.) ERIC ED581417.
report_number: EEF project: Success for All (SfA); ERIC ED581417; trial registration ISRCTN97011396
design: School-level two-armed cluster RCT (effectiveness trial), business-as-usual control (control schools paid GBP 2000/yr, taught standard curriculum). 54 primary schools randomised, 27 intervention vs 27 control (two cohorts: 39 schools randomised Jul 2013 + 14 randomised May 2014); 1767 Reception-class pupils (intervention n=874, control n=893). 7 intervention schools later withdrew. SfA = whole-school literacy programme (group learning strategies, phonics, assessment, structured daily lesson plans, leadership support; 16 days training/support over 2 years), delivered by teachers/classroom assistants trained by the Success for All Foundation. Pupils followed from start of Reception (pre-test) to end of Year 1 (24 months). Subjects/outcomes: literacy/reading (WRMT III Woodcock Reading Mastery Test, primary) and Phonics Screening Check (secondary, from National Pupil Database). England (mainly North/Midlands). Evaluation Sep 2013-Jun 2016.
problems: Registry/meta-analysis label is 'Sloan et al. 2018' but the actual EEF report is dated July 2017 with author order Miller, Biggart, Sloan, O'Hare (lead evaluator Sarah Miller; Seaneen Sloan is third author, Queen's University Belfast). This is unambiguously the correct study: it matches every registry attribute (School-level RCT, K-2 / Reception-to-Year-1, whole-school literacy with embedded teacher training delivered by Res/Dev = Success for All Foundation, short TPD duration, Average/High SES context, TPD goal 'Other'). The year discrepancy is a citation-convention issue on the meta-analysis side (no separate 2018 report exists on EEF; ERIC date is 2017-Jul). All reported effect sizes are explicitly labelled Hedges' g and were computed by the evaluators as the standardised mean difference from a two-level multilevel model (pupils L1 nested in schools L2; pretest BPVS as covariate), so they are BOTH pretest_adjusted=true and cluster_adjusted=true. The report gives g and its 95% CI but NOT the raw model coefficient/SE on the score scale; raw posttest means/95%CIs are given (Table 6) but raw SDs are not (only WRMT subscale SDs in Table 7, not the combined-score SD). Therefore impact_estimate/impact_se left null; g_se/g_var derived from the report's 95% CIs (g_se=(CI_hi-CI_lo)/(2*1.96)), which are the model-based cluster-adjusted intervals. n_t/n_c per outcome = pupils in the analysis model (Table 6 'n in model'). n_clusters=54 (schools). ICC: design/power-calc ICC=0.10; the realised analysis-stage ICC (Table 3, primary outcome at mid-point) = 0.13 (randomisation-stage 0.14) -- recorded icc=0.13 (NOT guessed; from Table 3). J small-sample correction ~1.000 (df in the thousands). PRIMARY outcome = WRMT Woodcock literacy at end of Year 1 (post-test, end of treatment) -> Reading; g=0.07 (Table 6). Earlier wave (Woodcock at mid-point, end of Reception) also extracted as a separate non-end-of-treatment timepoint (secondary timepoint). SECONDARY outcome = Phonics Screening Check at end of Year 1 -> Reading (phonics) ; g=0.06. FSM-eligible subgroups (Table 9) at end of Year 1 extracted as subgroup rows (is_full_sample=false). NOT extracted (sensitivity/exploratory, to avoid duplication): Table 8 (same model + school-attainment covariate: Woodcock post g=0.09, phonics g=0.06), Table 10 (low-baseline subgroup), 'on-treatment' analysis excluding withdrawn schools (Table 11: Woodcock post g=0.10, phonics g=0.07), multiple-imputation sensitivity (Table 13: Woodcock post g=0.08, phonics g=0.06), and fidelity-association analyses. All teacher/implementation (process-evaluation) outcomes skipped per spec. All student effects are small and statistically non-significant for the full sample. Primary outcome is academic (reading/literacy) -- NOT non-academic. Note: 226 (26%) intervention and 219 (23%) control pupils missing at the post-test (Woodcock); analysis-model n's reflect complete cases.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Success for All (whole-school literacy programme + teacher training) vs business-as-usual control - full ITT sample
effect_sizes.test_name: WRMT III (Woodcock Reading Mastery Test III) total literacy score (Word Identification + Word Attack + Passage Comprehension combined)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of Year 1, end of treatment after 24 months)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's Hedges g (Table 6, main complete-case analysis): standardised mean difference = intervention dummy coefficient from two-level multilevel model (pupils nested in schools) adjusted for BPVS pre-test, divided by the outcome SD. g_se/g_var derived from reported 95% CI [-0.03, 0.18]: g_se=(0.18-(-0.03))/(2*1.96)=0.0536; g_var=0.00287. Raw means (Table 6): Int 82.3, Ctrl 77.6; combined-score SDs not reported (subscale SDs only in Table 7). J~1.000 (df in thousands).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.18 Table 6 (also exec summary p.5; Table 8 with extra covariate gives 0.09)
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY confirmatory outcome at end of treatment (end of Year 1). Literacy/reading -> Reading. ~1 month additional progress, p=0.14, non-significant. EEF security 3/5 padlocks. Multilevel model fully accounts for school clustering. Headline value used in exec summary.
